title: Customer-facing maintenance + Terraform playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc contains: 1) customer-facing maintenance and SLA/SLO communication templates tailored for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, 2) Terraform module notes and minimal runbook for rolling upgrades, and 3) an internal upgrade checklist and rollback play.

Audience:
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success (primary)
- Eng private-deployments team (operators)
- Account security / legal (as needed for high-impact windows)

High-level goals:
- Provide reproducible, adjustable templates for notices (email/portal/SMS) for low/moderate/high-impact maintenance
- Define SLO behaviour during windows and how to credit customers (error-budget handling)
- Capture Terraform-specific steps and state migration notes for on-prem upgrades
- Lightweight internal checklist to avoid last-minute surprises

SLA / SLO guidance (private deployments):
- Baseline SLOs (example):
  - Uptime: 99.9% monthly for API endpoint responding to /v1/generate (excludes scheduled maintenance windows > 15 min)
  - Latency: p95 <= 450ms for inference small-models (documented per-customer profile)
  - Error rate: <= 0.5% 4xx/5xx combined (rolling 30d)
- Maintenance exceptions: Scheduled maintenance windows (announced 14 days / 72 hours / 24 hours pre) that are <= 4 hours do not count against uptime SLO if customer accepted notice or if a waiver is in the contract. Anything > 4 hours requires account manager approval and potential SLA credits.
- Error budget consumption: If maintenance causes SLO breach, record event in incident tracker PD-ops-maint. Create a credit calculation: minutes outside SLO / total monthly minutes * monthly fee * reservation-factor (per contract). Keep the calculation template stored as spreadsheet (linked_artifacts).

Customer communication cadence (recommended):
- Initial heads-up (T-14 days): purpose, expected impact, rough ETA window, contact for questions, opt-out instructions (if supported).
- Reminder (T-72 hours): more precise start/end windows, mitigation steps, staging info, and temporary request routing (e.g., route to fallback model / hosted fallback).
- Final reminder (T-24 hours): final scope, expected downtime or degraded levels, links to status page + runbook.
- During window: short updates at start, mid-point (if long), and completion.
- Post-maintenance: summary email with timeline, impact, validation metrics, and any follow-ups.

Templates (copy/paste and fill placeholders):
- Low-impact maintenance (no downtime expected)
Subject: Notice: Planned maintenance for your Redwood Private deployment (no downtime expected)
Body:
Hi {{customer_name}},

We will be performing routine maintenance on your Redwood Private deployment in {{region_or_vpc}} on {{start_time}} ({{tz}}). No customer-visible downtime is expected. We may restart background workers and briefly throttle non-essential async jobs for up to {{max_seconds}} seconds.

What this means for you:
- API endpoints should remain responsive; transient 429s are possible for <= {{max_seconds}}s
- We will monitor p50/p95 latency and error-rate; if anomalies are detected we will notify immediately

If you have a critical launch or blackout window during this time, reply to this email or contact your CSM: {{csm_email}} to reschedule.

Thanks,
Redwood Private Operations

- Moderate-impact maintenance (possible short downtime / degraded performance)
Subject: Planned maintenance impacting Redwood Private deployment in {{region}} — action recommended
Body:
Hello {{customer_name}},

We plan to deploy an upgrade to the runtime and underlying packages in your private deployment on {{date}} between {{start_time}}–{{end_time}} ({{tz}}). During this window you may see brief outages of up to {{expected_downtime_minutes}} minutes for inference traffic and brief increases in latency.

Mitigations we provide:
- Canary rollout and automatic fallback to prior model variant if errors exceed {{threshold}}
- Pre-run health checks and post-run verification script (we will share logs)

If this window conflicts with your business needs, please contact your CSM by {{reschedule_deadline}}.

Regards,
Redwood Private Operations

- High-impact / maintenance requiring scheduled downtime (>1 hour)
Subject: ACTION REQUIRED: Extended maintenance for your Redwood Private deployment on {{date}}
Body:
Hi {{customer_name}},

We need to perform an extended maintenance operation for your deployment that will require a planned downtime of approximately {{approx_hours}} hours to migrate state and apply a critical security fix. This work is scheduled for {{start_time}} ({{tz}}).

Please work with your internal stakeholders to confirm acceptance by {{acceptance_deadline}}. If we do not hear back, we will proceed at the scheduled time. If you require a different window, contact {{csm_email}}.

Impact details:
- API will be unreachable for the duration of the migration.
- Console access will be preserved for diagnostics, but operations are limited.

Post-maintenance verification: we will run a suite of smoke-tests and share the report via the status page and direct email.

---
Emergency maintenance: use a very short subject (EX: Urgent: Immediate maintenance for security vulnerability). Call + email and Slack CSM and SE. Follow escalation ladder in section below.

Internal escalation ladder (example):
- Level 1 (Operator): on-call private-deployments engineer (pager) — aim to mitigate within 30 minutes.
- Level 2 (SRE + SE lead): escalate if unresolved after 30 min. Communicate to CSM.
- Level 3 (Eng director + Legal): escalate for high-impact incidents or customer contractual escalations.

Terraform notes (runbook bullets & caveats):
- Always run terraform plan against a dedicated scratch workspace and apply only after peer review.
- State backend: S3 with DynamoDB lock for cloud-assisted private deployments; for air-gapped on-prem customers we rely on remote state bucket hosted in customer-controlled S3 or pre-approved object store. Confirm backend before any state migration.
- Provider versions: pin provider versions in module root. Example: terraform { required_version = ">= 1.4.6" } and provider "aws" { version = "~> 5.0" }
- Module versioning: tag module releases with semver and include migration notes when state schema changes. Keep a migration helper script in /scripts/terraform-state-migrate.sh (link in linked_artifacts).
- Drift detection: run terraform plan and a custom drift-check script that validates KV cache snapshot sizes and GPU driver versions before upgrade.

Minimal upgrade checklist (pre-run):
1) Read release notes for module and runtime (linked_artifacts).
2) Confirm customer backup snapshot exists and is recent (snapshot_id: {{snapshot_id}}).
3) Validate that the customer's state backend is reachable and locks are not held.
4) Run automated pre-checks: smoke endpoints, latency baseline (p50/p95), error rates, model cache size.
5) Notify customer (T-72h and T-24h) using templates above.
6) Prepare rollback artifacts and a documented rollback plan (see below).
7) Schedule staggered rollout if multiple clusters to reduce blast radius.

Apply / upgrade steps (during window):
- Acquire state lock, apply module changes, deploy runtime container with new tag, run migration jobs (if any), and run post-deploy verification.
- If applying changes that touch storage or model cache layout, run the migration in a maintenance-only mode and verify with checksum.

Post-upgrade verification (must pass all):
- Smoke test suite (health endpoints 200 OK)
- End-to-end sample request through customer API: expected model output sanity checks
- Latency/throughput sanity: p95 within {{delta_pct}} of baseline or documented exception
- No new 5xx spike, 4xxs investigated and justified

Rollback plan (if verification fails):
- If immediate severe failure: revert to previous module tag and runtime image using pinned artifacts. Restore state snapshot if schema migration irreversibly changed state.
- Notify customer with short notice: "We are rolling back to the prior release to restore service; ETA {{eta_minutes}}"
- Post-rollback: run verification and create a post-mortem.

Customer credit / SLO remediation template:
- Capture time window, observed downtime, contract reference, and credit calculation. Use standard credit matrix: 99.9%–99.0% => 5% credit, 99.0%–95.0% => 10% credit, <95% => negotiation. (Sample only; legal must sign off per customer contract.)

Operational TODOs / open questions (notes to self):
- Add automated portal toggle so customers can acknowledge maintenance notices via a link (reduces email churn).
- Confirm whether any customers legally require 30d notice for infrastructure changes (some regulated industries).
- Automate the post-upgrade verification reporting into the status page (PD: STATUS-impl ticket).

Appendix: quick copy snippets for Slack/Status page
- Slack (start of window): "Maintenance started for {{customer_name}} (deployment {{id}}). Impact: {{impact_summary}}. Contact: {{on_call}}."
- Status page short: "Planned maintenance — {{customer_name}} — started at {{start_time}}. Estimated end: {{end_time}}."

Example use-case (short):
- Customer reports intermittent 502s after driver update. Plan: schedule maintenance window T+7 days, run canary on 10% nodes, if green rollout remainder; if not, rollback and open ticket with driver vendor.

Last updated notes:
- Drafted by Aisha Patel. Comments welcome. Next review with CSM + legal on 2025-02-20.
